prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create one friendly, abstract, clear comic chemistry learning-goal illustration, PNG, landscape approximately 16:9, around 1600 by 900 pixels. Use warm white background, large rounded outlined ion spheres, orange sodium ions and teal chloride ions, a little gentle texture, approachable hand-drawn classroom style, not photorealistic and not a sterile technical blueprint. Main subject: a large three-dimensional NaCl crystal lattice fragment. Clearly highlight ONE central orange Na⁺ ion and EXACTLY SIX directly neighbouring teal Cl⁻ ions arranged octahedrally: above, below, left, right, toward the viewer and behind the centre. Use an oblique 3D view so the front and back neighbour remain visibly separate and countable. Show the crystal continuing beyond this local group as a subtle alternating grid fragment, so the drawing unmistakably represents a lattice fragment rather than an isolated NaCl₆ molecule. No covalent sticks or molecule bonds; light dotted direction guides may indicate neighbouring positions. Both negative ions and positive ions belong to one continuing alternating ionic solid. Use only a very few large readable labels: 'Ionengitter', 'Na⁺', 'Cl⁻', and '6 nächste Nachbarn'. The central plus and the six neighbour minus charges must be clear and correct. Put a small ordinary salt crystal on the table near the model for context. Avoid adding separate panels, electron circuits, tiny explanations, numbers implying concentrations, ionic mobility arrows within the intact solid, chemical reactions, extra decorative figures, logos or technical IDs. The six neighbours and 3D arrangement must remain easy to identify at 360px phone width; keep the model and labels large. This supports modelling and coordination reasoning; it need not show every material property in the same picture.
